The specification of a measurement model

Source: R/model-spec.R
model_spec.Rd

model_spec() returns everything bmm states about a model in one list of plain R data: its name and version, its parameters with their links and fixed values, the default priors, the ranges initial values are drawn from, the data columns it reads, and the names of its density and generator functions. Packages that build on bmm read a model here, not from the fields of the model object.

Usage

model_spec(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bmmodel'
model_spec(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bmmfit'
model_spec(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A bmmodel object, such as sdm(resp_error = "y"), or a bmmfit object returned by bmm().

...

Unused.

Value

A list of class bmm_model_spec with these elements, in this order:

name

The model's name.

package

The package that defines the model: "bmm" for the models bmm ships.

version

The model's version, such as "3par" for ezdm(), or NA for a model without versions. This is not the version of bmm.

domain, task

The research domains and the tasks the model is for, as listed by bmm_models().

citation

The references for the model, one per element.

parameters

A data frame with one row per parameter and the columns parameter, description, link (the link function, see link_transform()), fixed (logical), value (the value of a fixed parameter on the link scale, else NA), alternative_group (the parameters of which a formula may use only one, joined by "|", such as "criterion|bias", else NA) and softmax (TRUE for mixture weights that are transformed together through a softmax, whose link then does not apply on its own). For m3() with version = "custom" the formula defines the parameters, so the specification of the constructor lists b only and the specification of a fit lists them all. A model with variable precision (mixture2p(), mixture3p() or imm() with variable_precision = TRUE) is recognised by tau among its parameters; variable_precision and vp_nodes are not items of the specification.

default_priors

A data frame with the columns parameter, main, effects and sd: the default prior on a parameter's intercept, on its other regression coefficients, and on its random effect standard deviations, as Stan strings.

init_ranges

A data frame with the columns parameter, lower and upper: the range initial values are drawn from, on the native scale (softmax weights on the sampling scale). It has no rows for models that build their initial values otherwise (m3(), mpt()).

resp_vars, other_vars

Named lists of the arguments of the model's constructor, as the model was created with them: the response variables, and the other variables and settings. Values the constructor stores beyond its arguments are not listed. Expressions in them, such as the branches of mpt() trees, are given as strings.

data_columns

A data frame with the columns argument and role: what the data column named by each argument of the constructor must hold.

functions

A list with the names of the model's exported density and generator (random generation) functions, such as "dsdm" and "rsdm"; NA where a model has none. They are the model's exported d/r pair and may not cover every version: dmixture3p() and rmixture3p() do not express the item-wise precision of mixture3p() version = "slot_averaging" above K = set_size.

contract_version

The version of this specification, "0.9" until bmm 1.6.0 fixes it as "1.0".

For a bmmfit the list ends with one more element, bmm_version: the version of bmm the model was fitted with. Its name, domain and task are those of the installed bmm (the vocabulary of bmm_models()); the rest is what the fit was built with.

Every element is a character, logical or numeric vector, a data frame, or a list of these, so the list converts to JSON as it is. citation, domain, task and the entries of resp_vars and other_vars are vectors, which auto_unbox = TRUE writes as a single value when they have one element and as an array otherwise. An NA in a data frame row drops the key unless na = "null" is given. Use jsonlite::toJSON(spec, auto_unbox = TRUE, na = "null").

Stability

The specification is the stable surface of a bmm model for other packages (decision record 0005, "The model contract for companion and extension packages"): "The contract is exactly what model_spec() returns." and "The lifecycle rules apply to these items as they apply to exported functions. Reading the model object with $, its attributes, and internal functions stay outside the contract." A change to an element is announced in the NEWS under "Companion packages" before the release that makes it. Fields of a bmmodel object that model_spec() does not return can change in any release.

See also

Other model information: bmm_models(), parameter_info(), simulate_data()

Examples

spec <- model_spec(sdt_yn(response = "n_old", stimulus = "stimulus", n_trials = "n_trials"))
spec
#> Yes/No Signal Detection Theory Model
#> Package: bmm
#> Version: none
#> Parameters:
#>  parameter     link fixed value alternative_group
#>          d identity FALSE    NA              <NA>
#>  criterion identity FALSE    NA    criterion|bias
#>       bias identity FALSE    NA    criterion|bias
#>    sdratio      log  TRUE     0              <NA>
#> Use `$` for the default priors, initial value ranges, data columns and functions.
spec$default_priors
#>   parameter             main        effects             sd
#> 1         d     normal(1, 1) normal(0, 0.5) exponential(1)
#> 2 criterion normal(0.5, 1.5) normal(0, 0.5) exponential(1)
#> 3      bias   normal(0, 1.5) normal(0, 0.5) exponential(2)
#> 4   sdratio   normal(0, 0.3) normal(0, 0.3) exponential(2)
spec$functions
#> $density
#> [1] "dsdt_yn"
#> 
#> $generator
#> [1] "rsdt_yn"
#> 

# mixture weights transformed together through a softmax
model_spec(mixture3p(resp_error = "y", nt_features = "nt", set_size = 4))$parameters
#>   parameter
#> 1        mu
#> 2     kappa
#> 3    thetat
#> 4   thetant
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               description
#> 1                                                                                                                                                              Location of the von Mises distribution of memory responses (in radians). Fixed internally to 0 by default.
#> 2                                                                                                                                                                                                         Concentration of the von Mises distribution of memory responses
#> 3 Mixture weight for target responses. The weights of the target, the non-targets and guessing are normalised across the components present on a trial, with guessing as the reference, so thetat maps to the probability of a target response only jointly with thetant.
#> 4                                                                                                                              Mixture weight for non-target responses, summed over the non-targets, which share it equally. Like thetat, it is weighed against guessing.
#>       link fixed value alternative_group softmax
#> 1 tan_half  TRUE     0              <NA>   FALSE
#> 2      log FALSE    NA              <NA>   FALSE
#> 3  softmax FALSE    NA              <NA>    TRUE
#> 4  softmax FALSE    NA              <NA>    TRUE
